global_parameter.name: bank color
global_parameter.tooltip: color of the preset

global_parameter.name: led attenuation
global_parameter.tooltip: attenuation of the brightness of the led

global_parameter.name: usb audio
global_parameter.tooltip: what the minichord does with the sound of the phone or computer it is plugged into. 0: as it always has, it is offered as a speaker and what is sent to it is not played (a phone sends all its sound there, and goes quiet). 1: it is played through the minichord, beside the instrument, for playing along. 2: it is not offered as a speaker, so the phone or computer keeps its own sound. In every case the minichord's own sound can be recorded over USB. A setting of the instrument, not of a preset: it stays as chosen whichever preset is loaded. Changing to or from 2 restarts the minichord a moment later, since the phone or computer only learns what it offers when it connects

global_parameter.name: harp plate
global_parameter.tooltip: which harp plate is fitted, for the plates that are read between their zones. 0 is the stock strip, and any plate with twelve separate zones. 1 is zipper 24: a finger on the band between two zones touches both and plays the note between them, for 24 strings, the top one the band where the top zone meets an island of the bottom zone: two octaves of 12-EDO, or one of 24-EDO. The extra strings play in chromatic mode and the scale modes, which carry on up the scale; chord mode still plays twelve. 2 is the arcade wheel: its zones play as they are, and while a finger is on the ring it sends where, as control change 23 on the harp channel (0 at the top, counting clockwise to 127), with control change 24 at 127 as the finger lands and 0 as it leaves. 3 is the fretless wrap: twelve zones that taper into one another, with an island of the bottom zone above the top one; it plays as the stock strip does, and with harp ribbon the island is a thirteenth place, a whole octave in chromatic mode (zipper 24 wraps the ribbon the same way). Set it to 0 for any other plate: at 1 every other note goes missing, and at 3 a finger at the top with another on the bottom pad can read as the island

global_parameter.name: harp touch threshold
global_parameter.tooltip: how firm a touch the harp needs before a zone counts as touched; higher needs a firmer finger. 0 is the stock 40. A plate with smaller zones reads weaker and may want less. Takes effect once no zone is touched

global_parameter.name: harp release threshold
global_parameter.tooltip: how far a finger rises before a touched zone lets go: the zone lets go when its reading falls under this. Higher lets go sooner, lower holds on longer. 0 is the stock 20, and it is kept under the touch threshold. On the string plates it sets where on the way up pluck on lift sounds. Takes effect once no zone is touched

global_parameter.name: chord key signature
global_parameter.tooltip: automatically makes flat or sharp the chords for a particular key. 0=C, 1=G, 2=D, 3=A, 4=E, 5=B, 6=F, 7=Bb, 8=Eb, 9=Ab, 10=Db, 11=Gb, and the enharmonic keys 12=F#, 13=C#, 14=G#, 15=D#, 16=A#, 17=E#, 18=B#, 19=Fb, 20=Cb

global_parameter.name: sharp function
global_parameter.tooltip: change the sharp button to a flat button

global_parameter.name: transpose
global_parameter.tooltip: transpose all sounds by a number of semitones

global_parameter.name: temperament
global_parameter.tooltip: tuning of the notes: 0=equal, 1=quarter-comma meantone, 2=five-limit just (C major), 3=pythagorean, 4=werckmeister III, 5=kirnberger III, 6=vallotti, 7=young no. 2, 8=kellner, 9=sixth-comma meantone, 10=19-EDO, 11=24-EDO (quarter tones), 12=31-EDO. A keeps the master tuning pitch in the twelve-note ones, which are fixed to the keyboard, sweetest around C, so far keys sound progressively rougher, as they did historically. 10 and 11 divide the octave differently instead

global_parameter.name: master tuning
global_parameter.tooltip: reference pitch for A4, in tenths of a Hz: 4400 = 440.0 Hz, 4420 = 442.0 Hz. Range 432.0-446.0 Hz. Retunes the synth only; MIDI note numbers are unchanged
global_parameter.method: { int tenths = (value == 0) ? 4400 : constrain(value, 4320, 4460); float tuned_c_frequency = 130.81 * (tenths / 4400.0); if (tuned_c_frequency != c_frequency) { c_frequency = tuned_c_frequency; retune_active_voices(); } }

global_parameter.name: chord channel
global_parameter.tooltip: set the midi channel for the chord section

global_parameter.name: harp channel
global_parameter.tooltip: set the midi channel for the harp section

global_parameter.name: single port mode
global_parameter.tooltip: puts both the chord and the harp on the same midi port

global_parameter.name: MPE output
global_parameter.tooltip: gives every voice its own midi channel (MPE), so glide and the real pitch of a temperament or a divided octave survive the trip out; off is the usual single channel output

global_parameter.name: harp note-off on lift
global_parameter.tooltip: when a harp string's midi note ends. At 0 it lasts as long as the string sounds, through the release, so a strum arrives as ringing strings; a palm mute ends them all at once. At 1 it ends as the finger lifts, as before, leaving the release to whatever is receiving. With harp pluck on lift, at 1 it ends as the string starts to fade

global_parameter.name: MIDI in plays
global_parameter.tooltip: plays notes sent to the minichord over USB, as a sound module: on the harp's port and channel the harp strings (twelve voices), on the chords' port and channel the chord voices (four), the ones it sends its own notes on, by default the chords on port 1 and the harp on port 2, both on channel 1. Notes sound at their true pitch, whatever the preset's octaves and transpose, in the minichord's tuning and temperament; velocity sets their loudness, and a string's brightness; the sustain pedal holds them. Playing the minichord itself takes a voice back. Off, as a computer that echoes the minichord's own notes back to it would double them

global_parameter.name: knobs send MIDI
global_parameter.tooltip: sends the three knobs' positions out over MIDI as they turn, as control changes 20 (chord knob), 21 (harp knob) and 22 (modulation knob) on the chord channel, so they can be MIDI-learnt in a DAW or read by a program; the knobs keep doing their usual jobs

global_parameter.name: reverb size
global_parameter.tooltip: size of the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb high damping
global_parameter.tooltip: damping of high frequencies in the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb low damping
global_parameter.tooltip: damping of low frequencies in the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb low pass
global_parameter.tooltip: additional low pass in the reverb room

global_parameter.name: reverb diffusion
global_parameter.tooltip: diffusion within the reverb room

global_parameter.name: string spread
global_parameter.tooltip: fans the harp strings out across the stereo field, in percent of the full width: 0 keeps them all in the middle, as before. Centred on where pan puts the harp. How they are laid out is spread pattern

global_parameter.name: spread pattern
global_parameter.tooltip: how string spread lays the strings out. 0: by pitch, the lowest string to the left and the highest to the right, like sitting at a harp; ribbon and incoming notes land by their pitch too. 1: neighbouring strings on alternate sides, so a strum ping-pongs

global_parameter.name: chord ensemble
global_parameter.tooltip: a slow stereo chorus on the chords, the classic ensemble sound: a slightly swept copy on each side, moving at different rates, widens them and gives them a gentle shimmer. 0 is off, as before; 100 is half dry and half chorus

global_parameter.name: vocoder
global_parameter.tooltip: the chords (or the harp, see vocoder carrier) take on the shape of the sound coming in over USB, so they talk or sing with it: speech, singing or drums from the phone or computer. In percent of the vocoded sound in place of the dry; 0 is off, as before. The minichord has no microphone, so the voice has to come over USB, which needs usb audio 0 or 1 (0: only the vocoded chords are heard; 1: the incoming sound is heard too). With nothing coming in, the vocoded part is silent

global_parameter.name: vocoder carrier
global_parameter.tooltip: what the vocoder shapes. 0: the chords, the classic sustained vocoder sound. 1: the harp, whose plucks die away too fast to carry words well but make textures. 2: both, the harp's vocoded part coming through the chords' effects

global_parameter.name: vocoder consonants
global_parameter.tooltip: how much of the incoming sound's hiss (s, t, sh) the vocoder lets through, so words can be made out. 0 is a pure vocoder, only the chords' own sound

global_parameter.name: MIDI clock out
global_parameter.tooltip: sends rhythm mode's tempo out as MIDI clock (24 a beat), so a drum machine, a looper pedal or a computer plays in time with the minichord. 0 off, 1 on port 1 (the chords' by default), 2 on port 2 (the harp's), 3 on both. Only in rhythm mode: Start as it comes on (on the first beat of a bar), Stop as it goes off. Tap tempo and the default bpm move it. Nothing goes out while a MIDI clock is coming in: the minichord follows that one instead

global_parameter.name: pan
global_parameter.tooltip: pans the chord and harp sound, from fully separated to both in the middle

global_parameter.name: double tap control
global_parameter.tooltip: which setting two quick taps of the modifier button toggle, with the settings of double tap control 2 and 3 if assigned. 0 leaves this pair unassigned. Set it to 39 to switch chord layouts, or to any other setting you want under a tap. Set it to 256 for the looper: each double tap then takes its next step, record, play, stop, and record a new loop, instead of toggling; with double tap value 7, the step goes to a looper on the computer (the Lab's looper page) instead of the minichord's own (best given the double tap on its own, since every assigned pair moves on each double tap)

global_parameter.name: double tap value
global_parameter.tooltip: the value the double tap applies. Tapping again puts back whatever was there before

global_parameter.name: double tap control 2
global_parameter.tooltip: a second setting the double tap toggles at the same time as the first, so one double tap can turn a preset over to its other side. 0 leaves this pair unused

global_parameter.name: double tap value 2
global_parameter.tooltip: the value the double tap applies to control 2. Tapping again puts back whatever was there before

global_parameter.name: double tap control 3
global_parameter.tooltip: a third setting the double tap toggles at the same time. 0 leaves this pair unused

global_parameter.name: double tap value 3
global_parameter.tooltip: the value the double tap applies to control 3. Tapping again puts back whatever was there before

global_parameter.name: chord alternate control
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the adress targeted by the chord potentiometer alternate function

global_parameter.name: chord alternate range
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the control range of the chord potentiometer alternate function

global_parameter.name: harp alternate control
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the adress targeted by the harp potentiometer alternate function

global_parameter.name: harp alternate percent range
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the control range of the harp potentiometer alternate function

global_parameter.name: mod main control
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the adress targeted by the modulation potentiometer main function

global_parameter.name: mod main percent range
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the control range of the modulation potentiometer main function

global_parameter.name: mod alternate control
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the adress targeted by the modulation potentiometer alternate function

global_parameter.name: mod alternate percent range
global_parameter.tooltip: defines the control range of the modulation potentiometer alternate function

global_parameter.name: knob layer
global_parameter.tooltip: which functions the potentiometers play. 0: their main functions, and holding the modifier selects their alternates, as always. 1: their alternate functions, and the modifier only sharpens, so an alternate can be turned while chords sound. Assign the double tap to it (control 117, value 1) to switch layers while playing. After switching layers a knob waits until it reaches where its new function was left, so nothing jumps. While it is 1 the LED shows the preset colour pale
global_parameter.method: if (knob_layer != (bool)value) { chord_pot.pickup_on_next_switch(); harp_pot.pickup_on_next_switch(); mod_pot.pickup_on_next_switch(); } knob_layer=value; set_led_color(bank_led_hue, bank_led_saturation(), 1-led_attenuation);

global_parameter.name: hover control
global_parameter.tooltip: which setting a hand held over the harp plate moves, like a fourth knob: from as the preset has it with no hand near, to hover value with the hand close over the plate. 0 leaves hover unassigned. While the harp is played hover holds where it was before the hand came down, and after the hand lifts it waits for it to rise back to that height before following again; a quick swoop down to strum doesn't move it. Any setting a knob can take but the double tap's and USB audio. With knobs send MIDI on, hover also goes out as control change 25 on the chord channel, assigned or not

global_parameter.name: hover value
global_parameter.tooltip: the value hover control's setting reaches with a hand 2 cm above the plate, or nearer. It can be above or below the preset's own value, so hover can open a filter or close it, swell or duck

global_parameter.name: hover reach
global_parameter.tooltip: how high above the harp plate hover begins, roughly in centimetres; it is full at 2 cm. Further reaches higher but trembles more at the top, since a hand that far away moves the reading hardly more than the player's own movements do; nearer is steadier. Plates differ: one with smaller pads reaches less far

global_parameter.name: looper
global_parameter.tooltip: the looper: writing it does one thing and it goes back to 0, never kept in a preset. 1 record, 2 play, 3 stop, 4 clear, 5 overdub on or off, 6 the next step, 7 the next step sent to a looper on the computer instead (control change 90 over USB). Assign the double tap to it (double tap control 256) and each double tap takes the next step: record, play, stop, then record a new loop. With the double tap value at 7, each double tap works a looper on the computer, such as the Lab's looper page, and the minichord's own looper is left alone

global_parameter.name: chord alternate value
global_parameter.tooltip: nothing yet

global_parameter.name: harp alternate value
global_parameter.tooltip: nothing yet

global_parameter.name: mod alternate value
global_parameter.tooltip: nothing yet

global_parameter.name: firmware revision
global_parameter.tooltip: nothing yet

harp_parameter.name: global gain
harp_parameter.tooltip: global gain of the harp section

harp_parameter.name: scalar harp mode
harp_parameter.tooltip: what the harp strings play. 0=follows the chord (default), 1=Major, 2=Major Pentatonic, 3=Minor Pentatonic, 4=Diminished 6th, 5=Relative Natural Minor, 6=Relative Harmonic Minor, 7=Relative Minor Pentatonic, 8=scale chosen per chord, 9=as 8 but pentatonic, 10=your own scale rooted on the key, 11=your own scale rooted on the chord, 12=the generator scale rooted on the key, 13=the generator scale rooted on the chord

harp_parameter.name: custom scale
harp_parameter.tooltip: the scale used by scalar harp modes 10 and 11: tick the degrees you want

harp_parameter.name: generator
harp_parameter.tooltip: the interval the generator scale (scalar harp modes 12 and 13) is built from, in steps of the tuning: the scale is this interval stacked again and again and folded into one octave, which is how a regular temperament makes its scales. In 31: 7 with 9 notes is Orwell[9], 18 with 7 the meantone diatonic, 9 with 7 Mohajira (neutral), 10 with 7 Magic, 3 with 10 Miracle. In 12: 7 is the fifth, with 5 notes the pentatonic and 7 the major scale. Counted in steps of whatever tuning is chosen, so the same numbers make a different scale in another; past the top of the octave it wraps round

harp_parameter.name: generator notes
harp_parameter.tooltip: how many notes the generator scale has: how many times the generator is stacked. A chain that comes back to the root before it is done (4 in 12 closes after three notes) keeps the notes it has

harp_parameter.name: generator mode
harp_parameter.tooltip: which rotation of the generator scale the harp plays: how many of its generators lie below the root. 0 builds the chain straight up from the root; each step up moves one generator under it. With 18 in 31 or 7 in 12 and 7 notes, 0 is Lydian, 1 major, 2 Mixolydian, 3 Dorian, 4 minor, 5 Phrygian, 6 Locrian. Past the number of notes it stays at the last

harp_parameter.name: chromatic mode
harp_parameter.tooltip: puts the harp in chromatic mode, with static notes not dependant on chord selection

harp_parameter.name: harp rank
harp_parameter.tooltip: which twelve steps the chromatic harp plays, like the rows of strings on a triple harp: 1 is steps 1 to 12 of the division, 2 is 13 to 24, 3 is 25 to 36, carrying on past the octave where the division ends. 31 has three ranks, 19 and 24 have two, and in 12 there is only one, so this changes nothing there. Only in chromatic mode

harp_parameter.name: harp ribbon
harp_parameter.tooltip: play the harp as a ribbon controller: one fretless string along the strip, the pitch following the finger as it slides, gliding from each string's note to the next. Each finger sounds a voice of its own, and it sounds on touch whatever pluck on lift says. On the fretless plate, whose zones taper into one another, the pitch moves evenly along the strip; on the stock strip a finger mostly reads one zone, so the pitch rests on each note and slides where the finger bridges two (turn up ribbon glide to smooth the steps into a slide). In MPE the glide goes out as each voice's pitch bend; outside MPE the midi note follows the nearest string. A patch with some sustain holds a note under a still finger. Not on the arcade wheel

harp_parameter.name: ribbon span
harp_parameter.tooltip: how many strings the ribbon covers from the bottom of the strip to the top: fewer spreads each note wider and makes it easier to play in tune, more fits more range. 0 is the twelve strings of the plate, thirteen on the fretless wrap plate and zipper 24. In chromatic mode 13 is an octave and 25 would be two; in the scale modes the strings carry on up the scale. Chord mode has only its twelve

harp_parameter.name: ribbon snap
harp_parameter.tooltip: how strongly the ribbon holds to the strings' notes: this much of each string's width, in percent, plays its note in tune, and between the notes the pitch slides the rest of the way. 0 is fretless, 100 steps from note to note

harp_parameter.name: ribbon glide
harp_parameter.tooltip: how slowly the ribbon's pitch follows the finger, in milliseconds: longer smooths a jumpy reading and slurs fast moves, like portamento. 0 is the stock 10. On the stock strip, 60 to 120 turns its steps into a slide

harp_parameter.name: harp shuffling
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines different harp patterns. 0 is normal, 1 i with second, 2 is with fourth, 3 with sixth, 4 octaves, 5 chromatics and 6 useful when using a keymaster touchplate in Barry Harris mode

harp_parameter.name: octave change
harp_parameter.tooltip: changes the octave of the harp section up or down

harp_parameter.name: change held strings
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines whether a held harp note will change when changing chord

harp_parameter.name: amplitude
harp_parameter.tooltip: amplitude of the 12 initial oscillators

harp_parameter.name: string model
harp_parameter.tooltip: crossfades each harp string from its oscillator to a plucked string model, in percent. 0 is the oscillator alone, as before; 100 is the model alone: a burst of noise ringing round a loop the length of the string's period, which mellows as it dies away the way a real string does. Its pluck is brighter the harder the string is plucked (with touch velocity on), and it follows the ribbon's glide, the vibrato and the tuning. The envelope, filter and transient still shape it; an envelope with a quick attack and long decay lets the string ring as it would

harp_parameter.name: harp voice
harp_parameter.tooltip: what each harp string sounds: 0 its own synth (the oscillator and string model), as before; 1 piano; 2 pizzicato strings; 3 choir; 4 a string quartet (cello low, viola in the middle, violin high). A sample runs through the string's envelope, filter and level, so the preset still shapes it, and follows the ribbon and the tuning. Samples rendered by the midi-js-soundfonts project: the piano from FluidR3 (CC BY 3.0), the others from Musyng Kite (CC BY-SA 3.0); see lib/minichord_samples

harp_parameter.name: string decay
harp_parameter.tooltip: how long the plucked string model rings, in seconds for it to die away by 60 dB, at any pitch. Short is a muted, nylon or koto-like pluck; long a ringing steel string or a harp left to sound

harp_parameter.name: string damping
harp_parameter.tooltip: how much faster the plucked string model's highs die away than its lows: 0 keeps it bright and metallic as it rings, high mellows it quickly to a round, soft tone, like gut or nylon

harp_parameter.name: waveform
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines the waveform amongst 12 oscillators. In order: sine, sawtooth, square, triangle, bandlimited pulse, pulse, reverse sawtooth, sample and hold, variable triangle, bandlimited sawtooth, reverse bandlimited sawtooth, bandlimited square.

harp_parameter.name: attack
harp_parameter.tooltip: attack time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: hold
harp_parameter.tooltip: hold time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: decay
harp_parameter.tooltip: decay time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: sustain
harp_parameter.tooltip: sustain level of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: release
harp_parameter.tooltip: release time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: retrigger release
harp_parameter.tooltip: retrigger time of the envelope

harp_parameter.name: palm mute
harp_parameter.tooltip: lay a hand flat across the harp to stop every string ringing, the way a guitarist mutes with the palm: this many pads held at once reads as a palm rather than a strum. Pads under the palm stay silent until they are lifted, so the hand landing makes only a short muted chuck, but any other pad still plays: hold the mute with a few fingers and strum the rest. Another mute needs the palm lifted first. With pluck on lift, fingers placed on strings are a chord waiting to be played, so only pads that land together count, and a palm should be bigger than any chord you place: 6 or more A fingertip strum holds two or three pads at most, so 4 or 5 is a good start. At 0 there is no palm mute, as before

harp_parameter.name: palm mute release
harp_parameter.tooltip: how fast a palm mute stops the strings, in milliseconds: a few for a dead stop, longer for a softer damp. With harp pluck on lift, a finger on a ringing string stops it this fast too

harp_parameter.name: pluck on lift
harp_parameter.tooltip: when a harp string sounds. At 1 it sounds as the finger leaves the pad, the way a harp string does: touching a ringing string stops it, with the palm mute release, and nothing sounds while a pad is held. Strings can be placed ahead of time and lifted together for a chord or one by one for a roll, and since the note is chosen at the lift, placed under one chord and lifted under the next. A strum comes out a little later, by as long as the finger rests on each pad. At 0 it sounds as the finger touches the pad, as before

harp_parameter.name: touch velocity
harp_parameter.tooltip: how much a light touch plays softer and darker than a firm one: the harder a string is plucked, the louder and brighter it sounds and the higher its midi velocity. 0 plays every pluck the same, as before. At 100 a really light touch is quiet and dark (24 dB down, two octaves of the string filter, a tenth of the velocity), while an ordinary strum plays nearly full, about 5 dB down. Read from how firmly the finger lands: a quick tap or strum reads firm, a slow one rolling onto each string softer. Plucking on lift, from how firmly the string was held. Also the depth of touch pressure

harp_parameter.name: touch pressure
harp_parameter.tooltip: a held string follows how hard it is pressed, so the fingers shape the note while they hold it. 0: off. 1: follow: pressing harder than it was plucked swells it louder and brighter, as far as touch velocity reaches, and easing off lets it back down. A finger usually eases off as it lifts, so a note pressed up can fade a little before it rings out. 2: swell only: pressing harder swells it and it keeps the firmest it has been until it is let go, so it always rings out from there. Either way its pressure goes out over midi as it is, as each voice's channel pressure in MPE and as polyphonic aftertouch otherwise. Plucking on lift, held strings are silent, so it only sends on the ribbon

harp_parameter.name: strum velocity
harp_parameter.tooltip: how much a slow strum plays softer and darker than a fast one: the faster a strum sweeps across the strings, the louder and brighter they sound and the higher their midi velocity. 0 is off. With touch velocity on as well, each string plays as firmly as the firmer of the two says. A strum is neighbouring strings plucked one after another the same way; the first string of each has nothing to measure, so it plays by touch (full if touch velocity is off). On the stock and zipper plates, not the ribbon

harp_parameter.name: base frequency
harp_parameter.tooltip: corner frequency of the filter in the absence of control signal

harp_parameter.name: keytrack value
harp_parameter.tooltip: value that is multiplied by the note frequency and added to the base corner frequency to allow for keytracking

harp_parameter.name: resonance
harp_parameter.tooltip: resonance of the filter

harp_parameter.name: attack
harp_parameter.tooltip: attack time of the envelope filter

harp_parameter.name: hold
harp_parameter.tooltip: hold time of the envelope filter

harp_parameter.name: decay
harp_parameter.tooltip: decay time of the envelope filter

harp_parameter.name: sustain
harp_parameter.tooltip: sustain level of the envelope filter

harp_parameter.name: release
harp_parameter.tooltip: release time of the envelope filter

harp_parameter.name: retrigger release
harp_parameter.tooltip: retrigger time of the envelope filter

harp_parameter.name: filter sensitivity
harp_parameter.tooltip: sensitivity of the filter to the control envelope

harp_parameter.name: waveform
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines the waveform of the transient. In order: sine, sawtooth, square, triangle, bandlimited pulse, pulse, reverse sawtooth, sample and hold, variable triangle, bandlimited sawtooth, reverse bandlimited sawtooth, bandlimited square.

harp_parameter.name: amplitude
harp_parameter.tooltip: amplitude of the transient

harp_parameter.name: attack

harp_parameter.name: hold
harp_parameter.tooltip: hold time of the transient

harp_parameter.tooltip: decay time of the transient

harp_parameter.name: note level
harp_parameter.tooltip: level in the scale of the transient

harp_parameter.name: waveform
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines the waveform amongst 12 oscillators for the tremolo (amplitude variation). In order: sine, sawtooth, square, triangle, bandlimited pulse, pulse, reverse sawtooth, sample and hold, variable triangle, bandlimited sawtooth, reverse bandlimited sawtooth, bandlimited square.. Discontinuous signal will cause clicks

harp_parameter.name: frequency
harp_parameter.tooltip: frequency of the tremolo

harp_parameter.name: amplitude
harp_parameter.tooltip: amplitude of the tremolo.

harp_parameter.name: waveform
harp_parameter.tooltip: defines the waveform amongst 12 oscillators for the vibrato (pitch variation). In order: sine, sawtooth, square, triangle, bandlimited pulse, pulse, reverse sawtooth, sample and hold, variable triangle, bandlimited sawtooth, reverse bandlimited sawtooth, bandlimited square..

harp_parameter.name: frequency
harp_parameter.tooltip: frequency of the vibrato oscillation

harp_parameter.name: amplitude
harp_parameter.tooltip: amplitude of the vibrato oscillation

harp_parameter.name: attack
harp_parameter.tooltip: attack time of the vibrato envelope

harp_parameter.name: hold
harp_parameter.tooltip: hold time of the vibrato envelope

harp_parameter.name: decay
harp_parameter.tooltip: decay time of the vibrato envelope

harp_parameter.name: sustain
harp_parameter.tooltip: sustain level of the vibrato envelope.

harp_parameter.name: release
harp_parameter.tooltip: release time of the vibrato envelope

harp_parameter.name: retrigger release
harp_parameter.tooltip: retrigger time of the vibrato envelope

harp_parameter.name: pitch bend
harp_parameter.tooltip: continuous signal added to the envelope for pitch variation. 1 is the center, before will be negative pitch bending, after positive pitch bending

harp_parameter.name: attack bend
harp_parameter.tooltip: attack time of the pitch bend envelope

harp_parameter.name: hold bend
harp_parameter.tooltip: hold time of the pitch bend envelope

harp_parameter.name: decay bend
harp_parameter.tooltip: decay time of the pitch bend envelope

harp_parameter.name: retrigger release bend
harp_parameter.tooltip: retrigger time of the pitch bend envelope

harp_parameter.name: intensity
harp_parameter.tooltip: intensity of the vibrato and bend effect

harp_parameter.name: delay length
harp_parameter.tooltip: length in ms of the delay

harp_parameter.name: delay filter frequency
harp_parameter.tooltip: corner frequency of the filter in the delay loop

harp_parameter.name: delay filter resonance
harp_parameter.tooltip: resonance of the filter in the delay loop

harp_parameter.name: delay lowpass
harp_parameter.tooltip: lowpass component feedback into the delay

harp_parameter.name: delay bandpass
harp_parameter.tooltip: bandpass component feedback into the delay

harp_parameter.name: delay highpass
harp_parameter.tooltip: highpass component feedback into the delay

harp_parameter.name: dry mix
harp_parameter.tooltip: intensity of the dry signal in the output

harp_parameter.name: delay mix
harp_parameter.tooltip: intensity of the delayed signal in the output

chord_parameter.name: chord shuffling
chord_parameter.tooltip: defines different chord patterns. 0 is normal, 1 to 4 is one octave up with different additional notes, 5 is two octave up

chord_parameter.name: octave change
chord_parameter.tooltip: changes the octave of the chord section up or down

chord_parameter.name: glide chords
chord_parameter.tooltip: changes the glide lenght between chords

chord_parameter.name: chord inversion
chord_parameter.tooltip: voicing of the chord buttons. 0 is root position, 1 and 2 are the first and second inversions, 3 is the third inversion for seventh and sixth chords or the root position an octave up for triads

chord_parameter.name: chord spacing
chord_parameter.tooltip: how far apart the chord voices sit. 0=close (adjacent tones), 1=drop 2, 2=drop 3, 3=drop 2 and 4 (the most evenly spread), 4=spread the outer voices. Drops move a voice down an octave; a move that would leave the usable range is not made

chord_parameter.name: voice leading
chord_parameter.tooltip: place the chord voices to move as little as possible from the chord already sounding, the way a choir does, instead of building every chord upward from its root. 1 is on; 2 is strict, which also avoids parallel fifths and octaves, and the outer voices leaping into a fifth or octave, at the cost of a little more movement. Overrides the inversion setting while it is on. A slash chord keeps its bass on the note it names, in the octave nearest the chord already sounding, and the voices above it are led

chord_parameter.name: voice leading range
chord_parameter.tooltip: how far, in semitones, a voice led chord may sit outside where root position would have put it, converted to steps of the live division so it means the same interval in 12, 19 and 31. Small keeps the chords anchored where the buttons say, large lets them follow the previous chord further. Only used when voice leading is on

chord_parameter.name: slash level
chord_parameter.tooltip: level of the scale which will be affected when using slash chords

chord_parameter.name: slash voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: which of the four chord voices a slash replaces, counted from the bottom: 1 bass, 2 tenor, 3 alto, 4 soprano. At 0 slash level decides, as before. Bass is a slash chord in the usual sense, with the whole chord above it; the others change only that voice, for a melody note on top or a suspension inside the chord

chord_parameter.name: slash re-voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: with slash voice set to tenor, alto or soprano, the other three voices move to keep the chord whole around the slash note, as little as they can, instead of holding still. The bass always keeps the chord whole

chord_parameter.name: cantus
chord_parameter.tooltip: which chord voice the harp sets, the way slash voice lets a slash set one: 1 bass, 2 tenor, 3 alto, 4 soprano counted from the bottom, 5 whichever voice is nearest the note. The first string of each new harp gesture gives that voice its note (the rest of a strum does not). A chord tone keeps the chord whole around it; any other note is a passing tone that voice sings alone. It holds through a chord change when the new chord has the note, and lets go otherwise. A slash keeps any voice it holds. At 0 the harp leaves the chord alone, as before

chord_parameter.name: chord voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: what each chord voice sounds: 0 its own oscillators, as before; 1 piano; 2 pizzicato strings; 3 choir; 4 a string quartet. A sample runs through the voice's envelope and filter, so the preset still shapes it. Samples rendered by the midi-js-soundfonts project: the piano from FluidR3 (CC BY 3.0), the others from Musyng Kite (CC BY-SA 3.0); see lib/minichord_samples

chord_parameter.name: first note voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: what the first chord note sounds, in place of chord voice: 0 as the chord voice, 1 its own oscillators, 2 piano, 3 pizzicato strings, 4 choir, 5 a string quartet. So the notes can be different instruments, say pizzicato in the bass under a choir. Counted as the note levels (first note to fourth note) are: the first is the bass and the fourth the top with the chords voiced as they come, with inversions and with voice leading; chord spacing without voice leading can reorder them. Each note has its own sample player, so this costs nothing more

chord_parameter.name: second note voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: what the second chord note sounds, in place of chord voice: 0 as the chord voice, 1 its own oscillators, 2 piano, 3 pizzicato strings, 4 choir, 5 a string quartet. So the notes can be different instruments, say pizzicato in the bass under a choir. Counted as the note levels (first note to fourth note) are: the first is the bass and the fourth the top with the chords voiced as they come, with inversions and with voice leading; chord spacing without voice leading can reorder them. Each note has its own sample player, so this costs nothing more

chord_parameter.name: third note voice

Counted as the note levels (first note to fourth note) are: the first is the bass and the fourth the top with the chords voiced as they come, with inversions and with voice leading; chord spacing without voice leading can reorder them. Each note has its own sample player, so this costs nothing more

chord_parameter.name: fourth note voice
chord_parameter.tooltip: what the fourth chord note sounds, in place of chord voice: 0 as the chord voice, 1 its own oscillators, 2 piano, 3 pizzicato strings, 4 choir, 5 a string quartet. So the notes can be different instruments, say pizzicato in the bass under a choir. Counted as the note levels (first note to fourth note) are: the first is the bass and the fourth the top with the chords voiced as they come, with inversions and with voice leading; chord spacing without voice leading can reorder them. Each note has its own sample player, so this costs nothing more

chord_parameter.name: rhythm style
chord_parameter.tooltip: what rhythm mode plays. 0: the rythm pattern steps below, as it always has. The rest are written parts that follow whatever chord is held: 1 Alberti bass (lowest, top, middle, top in sixteenths), 2 waltz (oom-pah-pah, the bass alternating root and fifth), 3 boom-chick (root, chord, fifth, chord), 4 walking bass (root, third, fifth and a step into the next chord, under a Charleston comp), 5 boogie (root under a fifth rocking to the sixth), 6 Travis picking, 7 strummed guitar (down, down-up, up-down-up), 8 bossa nova, 9 arpeggio up, 10 arpeggio up and down, 11 ballad (bass held under chords pulsing in eighths), 12 reggae (chords on the offbeats), 13 6/8 arpeggio, 14 habanera. The first chord note is the bass part and the other three the chord part, each with its own note voice. Shuffle value swings them; voice leading makes the Alberti and the arpeggios move as a hand does

chord_parameter.name: rhythm bass
chord_parameter.tooltip: what the first chord note does under a rhythm style: 0 plays the style's bass part, 1 holds the chord's bass note as it does outside rhythm mode, 2 rests. Not for rhythm style 0

chord_parameter.name: rhythm chords
chord_parameter.tooltip: what the other three chord notes do under a rhythm style: 0 play the style's chord part, 1 hold the chord as outside rhythm mode (a bass line walking under a sustained pad), 2 rest (the bass line alone). Not for rhythm style 0

chord_parameter.name: rhythm follows hands
chord_parameter.tooltip: whether rhythm mode plays only while a chord is held. 0: it plays on, as it always has. 1: it sounds while a chord button is down and stops when you let go, the beat running on underneath so it comes back in time. 2: the same, and a chord pressed from silence starts the bar, as an Omnichord's sync start (not while following a MIDI clock)

chord_parameter.name: rhythm chord change
chord_parameter.tooltip: when a new chord comes into a rhythm style. 0: on its next note, and a chord pressed just after a beat (up to a quarter of a beat, 100 ms at most) still takes that beat. 1: on the next beat. 2: on the next bar, and a walking bass then steps into the chord waiting to come in. Rhythm style 0 keeps measure update

chord_parameter.name: rhythm articulation
chord_parameter.tooltip: how long a rhythm style's notes are held, in percent of their written length: lower is more staccato, higher more legato. Notes written to ring (the strummed guitar) ring until struck again whatever this is. Not for rhythm style 0, which has note pushed duration

chord_parameter.name: rhythm accents
chord_parameter.tooltip: how much a rhythm style's strong beats stand out from its weak ones, in percent of the written accents: 0 plays every note equally loud. Applies to the sound and to the midi velocity. Not for rhythm style 0
